final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with labor enforcement locked (automatic 30-day snapback, rotating inspectors, quarterly audits), sunset review framework finalized (six-year automatic extension unless objection), and auto rules phased at 65/70/75%. However, signature stalled pending Treasury compliance-cost validation and Canada's insistence on unconditional dairy access with Chapter 19 preserved.
minority_objections: Canada refused unconditional dairy concessions (fluid milk tariff-free six years) without Chapter 19 dispute settlement preserved
Dairy lobby demanded immediate market access or threatened to withdraw support for entire package
Supply-chain manufacturers refused to commit capex without validated Treasury numbers in writing before signature
key_conflicts: USTR's ultimatum for day-one 75% RVC vs. auto industry/Congress demand for phased implementation with validated compliance costs
Canada's dairy red line (supply management protection) vs. U.S. dairy lobby's demand for tariff-free market access
Signature timing: Canada/Mexico willing to sign with labor/sunset locked vs. Congress/industry requiring Treasury validation first
key_concessions: USTR accepted phased auto RVC (65/70/75%) after initially demanding 75% day-one across all vehicles
Canada offered limited dairy market access (fluid milk phased over six years) conditional on labor enforcement closure
Mexico accepted trilateral labor audit framework with automatic tariff snapback and no committee discretion
USTR locked sunset clause as six-year review with automatic extension (vs. hard termination)
red_lines: Canada: dairy supply management cannot be dismantled; Chapter 19 dispute settlement must be preserved
Labor unions: enforcement snapback must be automatic with zero discretion or no ratification support
Congress: labor chapter must have binding enforcement teeth or House Democrats walk
Auto industry: phase-in timeline and compliance costs must be quantified before commitment to retooling
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Chapter 19 dispute settlement was raised by Canada as non-negotiable but never substantively addressed by USTR or other parties
Treasury compliance-cost modeling became a blocking issue only after multiple rounds of negotiation on auto rules
Supply-chain capex freeze risk was flagged repeatedly but not integrated into signature-timing decisions
downstream_risk_variables: Treasury validation of 3-4% first-year labor cost could shift higher, killing Congressional support
Canada's Parliament ratification contingent on dairy protections and Chapter 19 preservation—both unresolved
Auto industry capex commitments frozen until Treasury numbers validated in writing
Dairy lobby threat to withdraw support if Canada does not concede market access unconditionally
uncertainty_notes: Treasury compliance-cost validation pending; Canada's dairy concessions conditional on Chapter 19 preservation (not addressed); signature timing unresolved (sign today with contingencies vs. wait for validated numbers); auto industry and supply-chain manufacturers withholding capex commitments until cost certainty achieved.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: Auto RVC thresholds (75% vs. phased 65/70/75%) drove multiple rounds of negotiation, forced USTR to concede phase-in, and stalled signature pending Treasury cost validation—directly shaped final package structure.
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Automatic 30-day snapback with zero discretion was Congress's explicit ratification condition ('Congress won't ratify a labor chapter that's just words'); drove Mexico's trilateral audit proposal and became locked text before any other element.
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada's dairy red line ('off the table—that's domestic political reality') forced conditional market-access offer and became explicit blocking issue when U.S. dairy lobby threatened to withdraw package support unless resolved.
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'stays in the trilateral—that's non-negotiable' but no other party engaged substantively; raised as red line but did not drive concrete proposal or concession in this meeting.
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset clause flagged as 'capex freeze' by supply-chain manufacturers; USTR locked six-year review with automatic extension (vs. termination) as direct response—became finalized text element.
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress explicitly conditioned support on labor enforcement teeth and validated compliance costs ('ratification fails if USTR forces 75% day one'); drove phase-in acceptance and Treasury modeling request—shaped negotiation path throughout.
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers repeatedly raised capex freeze and retooling costs as concerns, demanded validated numbers before commitment, but did not force a specific concession or proposal change—acknowledged but not decisive.
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's ultimatum ('ink the bilateral with Mexico this week and Canada negotiates from the outside') and Mexico's readiness to sign without Canada created explicit pressure that drove Canada's conditional dairy offer and acceptance of labor/sunset terms.
